passage: Vasudha slid off the top of the rope frame during PE and landed hard in the sand pit, one arm scraped open. Bidisha, who had finished the school first aid course in July, was beside her before the whistle stopped. “Don't sit up, Vasu. Stay still, look at me.” She pressed a clean folded handkerchief on the cut with firm pressure and sent Tarun running for Mr Gill and the nurse. Vasudha said her neck felt strange. Bidisha kept her hands off it and said quietly, “We won't move you. Help is coming. Breathe with me.” She counted slow breaths with her until Mr Gill arrived, the nurse close behind with the kit. Bidisha stepped back, told them exactly what she had done, and only then noticed her own hands were shaking.

qa.q: Who did Bidisha send to get help?
qa.a: Bidisha sent Tarun running for Mr Gill and the nurse.

qa.q: What was Vasudha probably feeling when she said her neck felt strange?
qa.a: Vasudha was probably frightened and unsure, since she spoke up about her neck while lying still in the sand pit.

qa.q: What could Bidisha do if no adult were nearby, and why?
qa.a: She could send someone to call the emergency number and keep Vasudha still and calm until help comes, because trained helpers are needed and moving Vasudha could make things worse.

qa.q: How might Mr Gill see what Bidisha did?
qa.a: Mr Gill would probably feel relieved and impressed that a student kept Vasudha still, pressed the cut and gave a clear report before adults came.

grounding: A teen trained in school first aid presses on a bleeding cut, keeps the injured person calm and still, and does not move a possible neck injury until adults arrive.

passage:
Dear Jatin Sir,
You told us at the end of the school first aid course to write if we ever used it. On Sunday I did.
My uncle was fixing the fan on the verandah when the ladder slipped. He fell and hit the railing. His forearm was cut and bleeding a lot, and he said his neck hurt.
I remembered two things you drilled into us. First, pressure. I folded a clean towel, pressed it hard on the cut and kept pressing, even when it soaked through; I put a second towel on top instead of lifting the first. Second, don't move someone who might have a neck injury. He wanted to sit up. I said, “Please stay still, Uncle, the ambulance is coming,” and kept talking to him about cricket to keep him calm. My aunt called the ambulance.
The doctors said his neck was only bruised. But they were glad nobody moved him.
Thank you, Sir.
Thomas

qa.q: What did Thomas do when the first towel soaked through?
qa.a: Put a second towel on top instead of lifting the first.

qa.q: What was Thomas probably feeling when the uncle wanted to sit up?
qa.a: Thomas was likely scared of doing harm but determined, gently keeping the uncle still and calm.

qa.q: Why is staying within trained limits important in a moment like this?
qa.a: Doing only what the course taught, pressure and keeping still, helps without risking harm while professionals handle the rest.

qa.q: How might Jatin Sir feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Jatin Sir would likely feel proud and moved that the course helped a student act calmly in a real emergency.

grounding: Shows a teen trained in school first aid pressing on a bleeding cut, keeping the injured person calm and still, and not moving someone with a possible neck injury.

passage:
Aadhya, you asked what the first aid course was actually good for. I'm Kamal, and I'll tell you about last Saturday in the park.
A man on a cycle hit the kerb near the gate and went over the handlebars. When I got there, his palm was cut deep and bleeding, and he was lying still, saying his neck felt strange.
I didn't try to be a doctor. I did the two things the course said. I pressed my clean handkerchief on his palm, hard, and held it, and when it soaked through I added my scarf on top without lifting. And I didn't let anyone move him. A man wanted to sit him up against the wall, and I said, “No, his neck, please wait for the ambulance.” My friend called the ambulance; I kept talking to him, asking about his dog, just to keep him calm and still.
Then the paramedics took over. That's it. That's what it's good for.

qa.q: What did Kamal press on the cut palm?
qa.a: A clean handkerchief, then a scarf on top when it soaked through.

qa.q: How might Kamal have felt when a man wanted to sit the cyclist up?
qa.a: Kamal was probably nervous about speaking up to an adult, but firm, worried that moving him could hurt his neck.

qa.q: What made Kamal's help useful rather than risky?
qa.a: Kamal stuck to what the course taught, pressure and keeping him still, and left everything else to the paramedics.

qa.q: What was it like for the cyclist to have Kamal there?
qa.a: The cyclist had someone calm talking about his dog, which likely eased some fear while waiting.

grounding: Shows a teen with first aid training applying pressure to a bleeding cut, keeping the injured person calm and still, and preventing him from being moved.
